analysis:
The supplied units are base-side excerpts (lines 473-1395) of docs/threat-model.yaml. The PR changes only the threat-model documentation, not runtime code. The patch excerpt shows a header comment added at head lines 46-49 and TB-012 rewritten in head lines 820-862. It also adds T-059 model-load fence text and a new T-060 near head lines 2349-2398. That head content is truncated in the supplied patch, so I could not read the new T-060 or the revised TB-012 detail.

The base excerpts cover TB-007 (cache storage), TB-009, TB-010, TB-011, the original TB-012 (base lines 812-841), T-007 through T-041, and T-041's SEC-035 cache posture. The base TB-012 is the part this PR edits.

I found no concrete security regression from the visible changes. A documentation edit adds no code attack surface, and the PR description says the changes record the operator mailbox, accept-time peer checks, the socket override, self-reported busy fields and a fail-open hold record. Those items describe behavior that may exist in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Addon/, which I did not see. The new mailbox and socket override are new local same-UID control surfaces. Their code and the A-018, TB-012, T-059 and T-060 definitions are outside the supplied evidence, so I flag this as an unverified integration question and not a finding.

Questions for the next pass:
- Does the head TB-012, T-059 and T-060 text accurately match the code in the Addon directory?
- Is the fail-open hold record's behavior (the effect of a corrupt or missing record) described faithfully?
- Does the coordinator treat self-reported busy fields as untrusted? The base header says coordinator handling is separate platform work.

None of the retained TB-007/T-041 cache text is changed in the visible ranges. The changed base ranges are 816-831 only.
